name: Sierra de la Madera (eastern slopes)
reasoning: Sierra La Madera is the Sky Island range in the municipios of Cumpas, Granados, Huásabas, Moctezuma and Villa Hidalgo (Bermudez-Enriquez et al. 2013, USDA RMRS-P-67). GeoNames 9028461 lies between those towns: 27 km east of Cumpas and 21 km west of Huásabas on the Bavispe (pipeline/measure/distances.py). The book puts the wolf on its eastern slopes, then across the Bavispe and north, which fits a range bounded on the east by the river. Readers disagree: Bell (2000) and Joe Hazelton's map take the other Sierra de la Madera, on the upper Bavispe (GeoNames 3996948), 81 km north-east. That range lies east of the river, so from it the wolf would reach the border without crossing the Bavispe, which the text has her do.

name: Crossing of the Bavispe
reasoning: The book names no crossing point. The Bavispe runs south along the eastern foot of the Sierra La Madera past Villa Hidalgo, Huásabas and Granados, so a wolf leaving the eastern slopes crosses it there; the point is on INEGI's channel of the river, and the circle reaches Granados and Villa Hidalgo. The Bavispe is one river bent into a long U: it flows north past Bacerac, turns west at Colonia Morelos and comes back south here. So her way north to the line at 108°30′ W must cross it a second time, on the eastern arm, which the book does not mention.

name: The border at 108°30′ W
reasoning: The book gives this exactly. West of 108°12′ W the boundary follows the parallel 31°20′ N (Gadsden Purchase, 1853), so the point is 31.33333 N, 108.5 W.

name: Whitewater Creek
reasoning: GNIS 896564: the only Whitewater Creek between the border point and the San Luis Mountains.

name: Animas Valley
reasoning: The GNIS pin for the valley is 108 km north, at 32.57 N. The stop is where her route from the Animas Mountains to the Peloncillos crosses the valley floor.

name: Foster Draw (the calf)

name: Starvation Canyon

name: Hog Canyon Springs
reasoning: GNIS 5857, Cochise County, 9 km from Starvation Canyon.

name: Between Clanton and Foster draws
reasoning: The high country between Clanton Draw (GNIS 887634) and Foster Draw (GNIS 889164), which lie 3 km apart.

name: Robertson's crossfence
reasoning: Between the Cloverdale Creek road and the Guadalupe pass. The Robertson family ran the Cloverdale Ranch from the early 1900s (Range Magazine, winter 2000, rangemagazine.com/archives/stories/winter00/bootheel.htm), so the fence is likely theirs. GNIS has no Robertson ranch and the ranch's bounds are not known here; the circle covers the ground between the road and the pass.

name: Low pass in the easternmost Guadalupes
reasoning: The east flank of the Guadalupe Mountains (GNIS 920606), where a pass would lead south-west toward the boundary.

name: Ranch house on the volcanic plain
reasoning: Past the Guadalupe pass and before the boundary. The book crosses a broad volcanic plain here. The Geronimo–San Bernardino volcanic field covers the northern San Bernardino Valley in basalt, from Cochise County into Hidalgo County and Sonora (New Mexico Geological Society guidebook; Arizona Geological Survey), which is the ground south-west of the pass. The ranch house itself is unnamed.

name: The boundary, a monument in sight
reasoning: Boundary monuments stand along 31°20′ N here. The circle covers the stretch south of the volcanic plain and north of the Cajon Bonita.

name: Down the Cajon Bonita
reasoning: The book spells it Cajon Bonita. GeoNames 4016262, the Cajón Bonito nearest the boundary; the other two are 89 km and 122 km away.

name: Passes of the Sierra de la Cabellera
The river crossing (the deputies)
reasoning: GeoNames 4013341 (named Oaxaca), on the Bavispe 19 km from Colonia Morelos. Colonia Oaxaca (El Marquesote) in Chihuahua, 89 km east, is a different place.

name: The mud-house settlement
reasoning: Unnamed. Between the crossing at Colonia Oaxaca and Colonia Morelos.

name: The hacienda
reasoning: Unnamed in the book. The text sets it on flat ground beside the Batopito River, with the road on the other side (1-10): the Batepito stream near Colonia Morelos (GeoNames 4017287), 1.7 km from the circle's centre. The circle is sized to the reach within a day of Morelos and the Pilares Teras. Bell 2000 (p. 107) also puts the hacienda on this river.

name: Into the Pilares Teras
reasoning: The range point, GeoNames 8688585, Serranía Pilares de Teras, inside the Bavispe's great bend south of Colonia Morelos; the book does not say where Billy enters the range.
